card.headline: Frontier unit economics collide: Fable 5.1 cache cut vs Astra Fast surcharge vs Gemini 3.8 Flash intro cliff
card.claim: September 2026 frontier releases are rewriting agentic unit economics more than headline benchmarks: Fable 5.1 keeps $10/$50 list but cuts cache reads to $0.25/M; GPT-6 Astra lists at $10/$50 (Fast mode 2× on short-context tokens); Gemini 3.8 Flash holds $0.75/$3.75 intro through 2026-12-31 then doubles to $1.50/$7.50.
card.one_sentence_take: Three verified pricing regimes landed in days — which becomes the default agentic spend lane this quarter is Contested between economics and capability/harness claims.
bullets: Primary: Anthropic — Fable 5.1 $10/$50; cache reads $0.25/M (75% cut); vendor estimates ~25% typical / ~45% highly agentic savings vs Fable 5.
Primary: OpenAI pricing — gpt-6-astra short-context $10/$50; Fast mode priced at 2× ($20/$100); cached input $1.00/M (4× Fable cache reads).
Primary: Google — Gemini 3.8 Flash intro $0.75/$3.75 through 2026-12-31; standard $1.50/$7.50 from 2027-01-01 (blog + API pricing page).
Specialist tension: list-price winner (Flash) can lose on cost-per-task if token intensity rises; Fable cache economics win only with high hit rates / stable prefixes.
Decision surface stays open: build/buy/ship default for agentic production spend — not settled by benches alone.
card.explainer: CIO pressure-test (2026-09-16): three-lane price facts corroborate across independent Primary pages. Contested is the decision frame — whether cache/intro/Fast economics dominate lane choice (Leg A) or capability/harness/distribution claims dominate and pricing is noise (Leg B). No averaged 'winner.' High is withheld on the decision; price facts alone would clear High.
card.point: Unit economics moved in footnotes (cache, Fast, intro cliffs) as much as in model cards.
card.motive: Labs want share of agentic spend; buyers want cost-per-task certainty before locking a default stack.
card.bottom_line: Recalculate cost-per-task with your cache-hit and token-intensity profile before naming a default — list price alone misleads.
card.blind_spot: No independent same-harness cost-per-task across all three lanes; Anthropic savings and Google diligence/token-intensity claims are still mostly vendor- or analyst-mediated.
blind_spots: No independent same-harness cost-per-task across Fable / Astra / Flash.
Anthropic 25–45% savings are vendor measurements on August 2026 usage mix.
Astra long-context tier ($20/$75 short→long) omitted from the simple three-lane slogan.
Gemini intro cliff may induce lock-in or migrate-before-Jan behavior not yet observable.
card.displace_what: Model-card / benchmark screenshot cycles that ignore list price, cache economics, and published intro cliffs
card.why_in: Named decision surface (default agentic spend lane) + second-order path (cost-per-task reshapes what ships) inside P0
card.why_out: Would kill if primary pricing pages failed to corroborate the three-lane economics or story collapsed to vendor benches only — did not happen

contested_legs.claim: Economics dominate: cache cut / Fast surcharge / intro cliff determine the default agentic spend lane this quarter.
Capability/harness claims dominate and pricing is noise — pick the lane that wins long-horizon coding / agent evals even at higher list price.

cio_pressure_test.price_facts: High — three independent Primary pricing/launch pages corroborate CSO draft numbers
cio_pressure_test.decision_frame: Contested — Legs A/B both live; never averaged
cio_pressure_test.high_withheld_reason: Default lane choice is not settled by receipts; only the pricing facts are
